about: The lists-folder sync engine, which exists twice: desktop/sync-core.ps1 (Windows) and local/engine.mjs (Linux, macOS).
Rows: {"p": project id, name, pos, deleted?} and {"t": task id, "in": project id, pos, text, parent?, status?, due?, notes?,
deleted?}. lists: the files in the lists folder (".trash/..." inside lists/.trash; "busy": written a moment ago). files:
project id -> file name. plan: with the base S (what the files reflect) and the server rows R, build the plan that makes
the files match R and apply it; after = every file in the folder afterwards (lists/.trash aside: "trash" lists the start
of each file name there). diff: with base S (ts 100), read the folder and queue changes; changes = [kind, id, field,
value, {base?, ts?}?] (any order; base / ts checked when given), with "guarded" (deletes held back) and "skipped" (some
list was not usable, or one is briefly missing) when given. State before the diff: "missing" (project id -> seconds its
list has been missing), "planned" (task id -> {age: seconds since the plan, added?, addedTs?, fields: {field: [value
before the plan, its ts]}}), "guard" (keys held back last time), "allow" (the user confirmed them) and "expected"
(keys of deletes made in the app, never held back); "guardAfter": the keys held back afterwards. restore ("Restore
them" under Deletions paused): with base S, the folder and "guard" (the keys held back), build the restore plan (only
for "keys" when given: a vanished list written again by itself) and apply it; "count" = tasks put back, after /
filesAfter as for plan. replay: whole sync cycles against a server that has S, with the clock "cycles" seconds after
the start for each; afterwards every file is "after", nothing is held back, no delete reached the server, and the

plan.name: a task moved to another list takes its subtask along
a list renamed elsewhere: the file is renamed
a list renamed only in letter case: the same file gets the new name, not a copy "Work (2)"
a new list from elsewhere becomes a file with its tasks in order
a list deleted elsewhere moves to lists/.trash
a list saved with CRLF keeps CRLF when a change from elsewhere is written
a new list whose name is taken by a local-only file gets " (2)"

diff.name: edits to text, status, deadline and notes become field changes

  > a note
- [ ] B ^bbbbbbbb

diff.name: moving one line gives only that task a new position
indenting a line makes it a subtask
a heading ends the nesting above it
a removed line becomes a delete
a new line (already with an id) becomes a new task after its sibling
a renamed file keeps its project and renames it
a list moved to lists/.trash (how the apps delete one) deletes its project; its tasks stay with it, restorable
the tab order of the lists folder becomes project positions
an impossible deadline in the file is sent as no deadline
control characters in a line are not sent
a CRLF file is read like any other
a list being written right now is left alone: no changes, no deletes
most tasks vanishing at once pauses the deletes
a list gone for a moment is no delete yet (moved out and back, a sync client re-downloading the folder)
a list gone for two cycles and 10 seconds is held back, however small: only lists/.trash says a list was deleted
a list shared with others gone for good is held back too, and so is an empty one (nothing to count, still not deleted)
every task of a list gone at once (its file emptied) is held back, however few
a list written over by another program: its new lines are sent, its old tasks are held back
the last task of a list deleted in the app (an expected delete) is a delete
a list of 5+ tasks gone for good waits for a confirmation
most of one list vanishing pauses the deletes, even when few tasks vanish overall
a confirmation deletes what was held back; what vanished since is weighed again
a field put back to its value from before the last plan is sent as of then: the other device's edit stays, this one is kept as a conflict
another edit of a field the last plan changed counts as made alongside it (newest wins, the other is kept)
a task the last plan brought in, dropped by a save from an older copy, is a conflict (dated before it arrived), not a delete
a task an older copy puts back under its old parent goes back to the plan's place (dated before it)
half an hour after a plan, an edit is an edit again

restore.name: an emptied list gets its held-back tasks back: subtasks under their parents, deadlines with a time, notes, statuses, ids
